source: Adapted from Serious Eats / J. Kenji López-Alt
notes: Might benefit from a squeeze of lemon juice — try it next time.

ingredients: 3 packed cups fresh basil leaves (~3 oz / 85g)
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
steps: Toast pine nuts in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, 3-4 minutes until golden and fragrant. Transfer to a plate to cool.
(Optional) Blanch basil in boiling water for 10 seconds, then transfer to ice water. Squeeze dry in a clean towel. This locks in vivid green color.
Add garlic and cooled pine nuts to the food processor. Pulse 8-10 times until coarsely chopped.
Add basil leaves and 1/2 tsp salt. Pulse 10-15 times until broken down but still slightly textured — don't purée.
With the motor running continuously, pour olive oil in a slow, steady stream through the feed tube. Process just until combined, about 15 seconds.
Transfer to a bowl. Fold in the parmigiano and pecorino by hand with a spatula. (Processing the cheese in the machine can make it gummy from the heat.)
recipe.serving: Cook 1 lb pasta (trofie, linguine, or gemelli are traditional). Reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining. Toss pasta with pesto, loosening with pasta water a few tablespoons at a time. Never heat the pesto directly in a pan — the basil will turn dark and bitter.
recipe.storage: Fridge: press plastic wrap onto the surface, drizzle olive oil on top, keeps 4-5 days. Freezer: spoon into ice cube trays, freeze solid, transfer to a bag — keeps 3+ months.
